The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a7ab4d86183890be), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 141-142. statement: Fix an inner algebraic template, and replace the compatible-pair list by the list of all ordered pairs of point-track types in (8.5). The two positions remain independent even when the types coincide; no line-product blocks are added. 141 Rebalance all blocks by the repetition construction of Section 8.2. This encoding has polynomial length and a uniform polynomial-time construction, and has the following properties. (i) Valid canonical words have constant distance and the perfectly complete smooth tester and proximity guarantee of Proposition 8.5. A structurally canonical word whose label is invalid has rejection probability at least one fixed θinv > 0. (ii) One fixed radius permits arbitrary fixed average accuracy for bounded-density requests, with joint pair density for products, arbitrary public masks and forms, and all-hypothetical-branch smoothness as in Proposition 8.10 and Lemma 8.11. (iii) From a sufficiently small fixed neighborhood of any structurally canonical word, its entire logical tape b = (w, e, (si)i) is recoverable exactly in deterministic polynomial time, whether or not that tape is valid. The constants and the radius may depend on the whole fixed template and its block list. No common one-port layout or radius fixed before arity is asserted for this variant. More generally, the same binary transfer applies to a supplied fixed finite chart template with the field, degree, slot, and polynomial-size bounds used in Section 8, subject to these explicit conditions: its canonical recipes are defined also on invalid logical tapes; its bounded binary-form algebraic validator has perfect completeness and an exact constant gap on genuine degree-in-bound polynomial tuples; its linear probes have bounded point marginals and its products have independent full point marginals; and its order-one grid charts and constant mode/marker tensors separate labels. Full logical recovery requires order-one grid charts for every logical coordinate. This transfer assumes these algebraic properties; it does not assert that the fixed-input path of Section 7 realizes an arbitrary macrograph.
